Err. Long post man. Sorry. Ive been down this road before and here is what I have to say as an experienced IT dude with a lot of pain and suffering put into my own gear to make it as awesome as possible.

[tldr; ditch the laptop. Build a gaming PC for a good price that will last 3-5 years. Get a cheap laptop that will work for classes for about the same amount of time]

I hate to say it but I agree with /u/Secus I have owned 2 gaming laptops. I was one of the officers for the PCGamers club for my campus for several years (server/network/etc). Gaming laptops do not hold up. No matter who builds them.

I would suggest that you track the overall temp's in the system and when they start to climb even with you using the same cooling that you immediately replace your thermal paste (This may require full disassembly of the system). It means that its drying out and will become increasingly less effective. Ive had a lot of good luck with Arctic Silver (Still use it for my desktops) .. Not sure what is out there these days. I gave up on "gaming" laptops ages ago.

The primary problem comes with how the GPU is mounted to the motherboard (Funny thing, This is why the early PS3 got the yellow light of death and the xbox360 got the red ring of doom, ive fixed several because of this). If you build a desktop PC there is a lot of separation from the main board and GPU that allows for MUCH better cooling overall. This is mainly because you are basically plugging a big "daughter" board into a main board. There is often a lot of room inside the system's case for extra airflow as well as room for much larger fans. This is not the case in a laptop where space is a premium.

Laptop GPU's are typically mounted in "BGA" fashion (Ball Grid Array). This means that the GPU has a large amount of "pads/contacts" on its base. These are mounted to corresponding points on the motherboard. This is done by dropping a "ball" of solder onto the contact points then joining the two together with heat.

Over time this joint fails (This is partially because we are no longer allowed to use led based solder.. PM me for more info if you want).

This causes something called "Chip Creep". Basically, micro fractures cause some of the points to stop making contact. Luckily because we are using modern hardware a lot of these systems are somewhat resilient and will still function, just at a decreased capability. This will eventually lead to "complete failure" of the system as enough fractures will cause critical failures or odd voltages caused by the fractures will cook the chip. (this happened to BOTH of my gaming laptops).

(You can note that even if the system is not working properly.. If it heats up and then you restart it.. It starts working again. This is because the metal in the micro-fractures has expanded enough to make contact again. Cool stuff, right?).

A stop-gap for this is that you "re-flow" the solder joints when you start to notice problems. I did this 3 times on each laptop. Extending their life by around a year and a half. This is a potentially destructive procedure that can either bring the laptop back from the dead... Or will insure its death. (Note, I fixed my ps3 4 times doing this. A friends xbox 360 2 times doing this.. Because they were already out of warranty).

I wish you the best of luck but my overall suggestion is to cancel your order. Build a gaming desktop for 4/5ths of the cost of the laptop and buy a cheap ass 200-300$ laptop to use for classes. Have an epic gaming computer for 4-6 years and a laptop good enough for school for the same amount of time.

What do they say about mixing business and pleasure ;) You often fail at both!
